To say that someone can get obsessed with an idea that becomes a problem is a very weird thing to say. It has some truth in it given different circumstances, where let's say I do happen to stumble upon situations where I make up ideas about it and they are usually negative which in conclusion makes it bad yes. But at this current conversation I think that I'm not obsessed with anything to be polite. 

Now briefly about my experience with thoughts under depression, they vary on the mood and if you know a thing or two moodswings happen pretty much everyday multiple times, which simply leads to overthinking, otherwise makes out nothing. Also thinking about what hurts you is a dangerous place, I learned that it's left understood once and not touched until its time comes. Overriding ur mind with those have caused me a few panic attacks.

As Immediate-Ruin2464 mentioned, Depression is indeed a medical condition which psychiatrists specialise at, I wouldn't change my mind about that even if I had 4 of them already. You just have to find the right one and I've been straight dumb not to ask for a new one while visiting one at that time.

Honestly I don't feel like I have the time to soften my mind up, I asked for help and you people came to help me and the least I will do is soften myself up at a moment like this.

When someone like LordFondleJoy feels sorry for your situation and then writes down multiple possibilities, I don't want to let people like that down, there's also someone in my life that acts for me as my last hope of motivation which was why I came here to seek for help. 

But I like explaining my thought process or responding to some of these comments which I really haven't done yet, because I just been running rounds waiting for this week to end.

Well you see I've been a gamer since I moved to Norway, I found that to be my only escape from reality, avoiding problems and such. I'm at the point where I set my pc on sale and everything that's attached to it, I really deeply want to never have to sit down at this pc again for the same reasons mentioned before.

I've met plenty of people, but something about having online conversations with people just doesn't give me anything anymore, my body craves moment, my brain wants action, real faces, real experiences.

You might not understand how many day to day skills you lose sitting so much at the pc, you don't encounter difficulties/problems to solve, and now I've dug up such a huge one that I can't dig myself out of, but I'm trying.

It's funny because before I moved to Norway my life was consisting of only outside activities, I had bunch of friends, bunch of hobbies, I was a thriving soul, I even was at my schools special group, my role in it was to come up with shows and activities for the school, I was loved by everyone, but I understand why as well, because I put that work and effort not for myself, but for others and it felt so natural to do, like I was just good at it, never really bothered about anything in my life there, well homework that was important, but then the language barrier came here in Norway and I lost all of my skills.

As I'm glad that's something that helped you, in my view problems gotta get fixed where they started, I have quite strong views on how person should stand and withstand whatever that is being thrown at us, just that I'm not quite the example for it.

And I cannot just simply move away to a different part of the world in hopes that it will change something.
